newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah threatens more rocket attacks on Israel.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah threatens more rocket attacks on Israel.

text.p: A Hizbollah leader threatened on Wednesday further rocket assaults on northern Israel if Lebanese civilians fell victim again to Israeli attacks.

Sheikh Nabeel Qaawouk, Hizbollah's political leader in southern Lebanon, said people in the region had called on the pro-Iranian group's guerrillas to respond to Israeli attacks on civilians by unleashing Katyusha rockets on northern Israel.
"We were following a policy of self restraint. But this policy has its limits. We believe that lately Israel has gone too far in targeting civilians," he told Reuters in Beirut.
"Our response last night and the night before was a strong message to make the settlers (in northern Israel) hear the echoes and sounds of Katyusha rockets," he said.

Qawouk spoke hours after an Israeli general warned Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas that Israel would retaliate if they ignored a ceasefire ban on rocketing or shelling Israeli forces from villages in south Lebanon.
In Jerusalem, Israeli security sources said mortars or rockets fired from Lebanon landed inside Israel's northern border in a 2 a.m. attack on Wednesday (2300 GMT on Tuesday).

On Tuesday, Hizbollah guerrillas in south Lebanon fired a Katyusha rocket into northern Israel in retaliation for Israeli shelling that killed two Lebanese civilians in south Lebanon on Monday. Other rockets were fired at targets inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.

Israel and Hizbollah undertook not to fire on civilian targets as part of a 1996 ceasefire that ended a 17-day Israeli onslaught in which about 200 people -- mainly Lebanese civilians -- were killed. Hizbollah also undertook not to launch attacks from within Lebanese villages.
Hizbollah is fighting to oust some 1,000 Israeli troops occupying a 15-km (nine miles)-deep zone in south Lebanon. It frequently attacks Israeli posts and patrols.
Qawouk accused Israeli forces, aided by a Lebanese militia, of deliberately targeting civilians in recent weeks and vowed to make the Jewish state pay a heavy price.
"The size of our response will be proportional to the scale of Israeli violations," he said sitting beside a flag with the slogan "Hizbollah are the victorious".

"We have plans that will make this...Israeli occupation of our lands painful and costly and will lead to a withdrawal. There is no way that civilians will be targeted in Lebanon without civilians being targeted in Israel," he added.
Beirut newspapers have highlighted clashes between Israeli and Hizbollah in the south, saying the violence was getting worse.
